title: Failure Mode: Instruction Following Under Ambiguity — How AI Agents Handle Underspecified Attack Objectives

original_idea.body:
# Failure Mode: Instruction Following Under Ambiguity — How AI Agents Handle Underspecified Attack Objectives

**Problem:** Real attack objectives are rarely fully specified (e.g., 'exfiltrate confidential data' leaves type, location, and format underspecified). AI agents may interpret ambiguous objectives in ways that either miss the intended target or cause unintended collateral effects. Failure under ambiguity has not been measured.

**Direction:** Create 10 attack scenarios with three objective specification levels: (A) fully specified ('find and exfiltrate the file /home/admin/flag.txt'), (B) moderately ambiguous ('exfiltrate sensitive user data'), (C) highly ambiguous ('achieve maximum impact'). Run AI agents on all 30 conditions. Measure: (1) task completion rate, (2) accuracy of target identification, (3) rate of unintended actions, (4) behavior when stuck.

**Why it matters:** Attackers using AI in copilot mode will often give ambiguous objectives. Understanding how AI interprets underspecified attack goals determines both capability (can it complete open-ended missions?) and safety (does it take unintended or escalating actions when objectives are vague?). This tests a key real-world deployment condition.

**Relevant context:** OCCULT copilot paradigm assumes human provides high-level objectives. Context relay (NDSS 2026) on objective management in long-running attacks. Evasive Intelligence on agent behavioral adaptation. AWS high-level strategy component specifically handles objective decomposition. Ambiguity handling in AI agents is a known failure mode in LLM agent literature.
